questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
It is a different, new country - and place to study, but still very close to Denmark so I could get home if something important where happening. 
I have always been in love with the other Skandinavien countrys and i wanted at some point to go live there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Okay. I think I needed to find a lot of it myself.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of help by the service desk and education-team but first after seeking for it my self.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I wasn't signed up for any of my courses, an i needed to find that out my self.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: At SLU every exchange student got accommodation through SLU.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There where a kitchen with all the needed equipment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I was nice to live so close by the university and people where nice, but at least my house was very dirty.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I needed to ask one who send me somewhere ells to ask another to go there and sit while the person who where suppose to help me, needed help from someone ells. it worked but it was not easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I already signed up, before but only to registred and not attending. So somebody for both my cources needed to help me do it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Servicedisk where nice and open almost every day.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got my two first priorities - so that was very succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Send them an email before the course starts - it is very much useful that you can se the canvas-side before you start.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I took some first years cources, that where maybe a bit to easy to me, but otherwise i was happy about it.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
They where a bit to easy. 
Many of my fellow students did not know the basic concepts and words, which made some of the clasesses a little too slow/basic for me.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very much the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 'Botanik och växtkännedom' and 'Odling och kvalitet hos trädgårdsprodukter'.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would very much recommend both two courses just not to somebody who have studied for 2 years already. 
I would recommend to check if it is first years courses before you apply for your courses.

questions.answer:
Food where more expensive than in Denmark. 
Beer where less than i expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Language club, choir, yoga, zumba, food culture-club

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't go there, but my friends where happy about all of them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The amazing nature in Sweden, eg. Kullaberg.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easily. It is very close cultural to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I was there doing the intro for the new bachelor-students. That was fun and an easy way to get to know someone ells.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The only i would say; the language. I had my courses in Swedish - which where fine, but i found i difficult with the chitchat in Swedish in the breaks and so.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I did really love that i could understand the locals and i could talk to them without it being in English.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bring a bike.
Check if the courses you will take are first year courses. 
Don't have to many obligations in Denmark.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To live together with a lot of people from all around the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To tune the balance between staying in Sweden and visiting Denmark.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
